capabilities.notes: Owned lifecycle and bounded join; successful native submission is not a connected callback. Mixing raw runtime ownership is unsupported.
Explicit service-wide string/numeric identity; token privileges must match.
Only combinations that preserve owned observers, lifecycle and publication contracts are supported.
Parameters are passed to the native SDK; a valid JSON object is not proof of option support.
Independent send/receive PCM formats; integral-millisecond input, caller/native timing limits, copied receive frames.
Codec packets only; no container demuxing or delivery guarantee. Named codec and multichannel expansion is tracked separately.
WaitPCM is a sent-byte/wall-clock estimate, not native drain or peer playback acknowledgement.
Current high-level path is validated compact CPU buffers. Extended layouts are tracked separately; no GPU handle support claim.
Encoded frames only; peer/native codec availability remains conditional.
High-level methods cover normal publication/subscription; manual subscription must be configured explicitly.
RTC data streams are distinct from RTM; local submission does not confirm recipient processing.
Owned observer delivery and bounded copied queues; detailed callback decisions/configuration are classified separately.
Extension-dependent external APM; pinned Linux archive lacks AINS, so initialization can fail.
Bounded request waits and ownership; cancellation stops waiting and does not roll back submitted native actions.
Messaging and user targets with explicit options; feature entitlements and peer delivery require integration checks.
Presence queries and copied state; legacy WhoNow/WhereNow map to equivalent query families rather than duplicated high-level method names.
Revision zero is forwarded unchanged; use explicit revisions and account for asynchronous completion.
High-level lock operations default to no native acquisition retry; explicit retry options are tracked separately.
Requires native/project history support and history-enabled publishing; binary messages are copied by explicit length.
Owned stream channels and partial-subscription results. Stream join/renew uses RTC tokens.
Copied event payloads with bounded drop-newest queue; request correlation is separate from that queue.
Borrowed native handles cannot outlive the callback, replace owned handlers, or release owned objects.
Pinned C callback ABI overrides unsafe upstream Go signatures; not drop-in source compatibility.
Slice callbacks retain every native array element; method status/request-ID fixes are listed individually in exceptions.
Binary metadata is copied; audio profile/scenario and volume indication keep native behavior and limits.
Exposes native keyframe requests, encoder configuration and simulcast; no claim that native codecs accept every configuration.
Received-audio VAD v2 is separate from standalone native VAD and external APM; 16 kHz mono per-user receive constraints apply.
Copied native encryption configuration is applied during setup; interoperability and privileges need a live check.
High-level entry points exist with and without avcodec; actual decoding requires optional FFmpeg libraries. Acceptance does not report asynchronous decode/send completion.
Pure packet helpers are retained in raw package; they are not an end-to-end SEI transport guarantee.

Not yet integrated in this worktree: typed role transitions, synchronous audio decisions/formats, idle release, local access point and extensions. Promote only after public APIs and tests are present.
Not yet integrated in this worktree: explicit CPU stride/crop/color/alpha, additional codec fields, typed track controls and owned standalone VAD. GPU/hardware input remains excluded.
Not yet integrated in this worktree: typed identity/native configuration, presence-only subscriptions, exclusion/retry options and opt-in complete result events.

Media player, RTMP publishing and device APIs are not in official Go v2.6.5. C++-only RTM stream parameters/timestamps and hardware-video marshalling lack corresponding pinned Go/C surfaces; these are not lost official-Go methods. Extensions/codecs remain conditional.

Retained low-level constructors, converters, resource methods and advanced calls with manual ownership. Tests exercise selected invalid-handle paths, not every callable or live behavior; signature retention is not high-level feature parity.
